groups.principle: Use of processors offering sufficient guarantees
groups.reason: The policy requires all processors to sign a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) before handling personal data, ensuring they commit to GDPR compliance. International processors use approved safeguards (SCCs, adequacy decisions, BCRs), demonstrating sufficient guarantees.

sub_obligations.reason: The policy requires all processors to sign a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) before handling personal data, ensuring they commit to GDPR compliance. International processors use approved safeguards (SCCs, adequacy decisions, BCRs), demonstrating sufficient guarantees.

evidence.quote: All processors are required to sign a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) prior to receiving any personal data.

Some of our processors are located outside the European Economic Area (EEA). Where data is transferred internationally, Acme relies on the following safeguards: Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) approved by the European Commission, Adequacy decisions where applicable, Binding Corporate Rules (BCRs) where relevant.

groups.principle: Flow-down of obligations to sub-processors and processor liability
groups.reason: The policy evidence mentions that Acme engages third-party processors and requires them to sign a DPA, but does not contain provisions confirming that the *same* data protection obligations are flowed down to sub-processors engaged by those processors. The supplied company policy evidence contains no statements regarding the initial processor's full liability to the controller for a sub-processor's failure to fulfill its obligations.
